seo.title: Cropstar — software that explains instead of prescribes
seo.description: Open-source farm software for regenerative agriculture. Every number carries its uncertainty, its source and its drivers. Scenarios, never recommendations.
seo.ogTitle: Cropstar — understand your field, decide for yourself
seo.ogDescription: Open-source farm software for regenerative agriculture. Learning by doing, with the consequences made visible.

hero.title: Understand your field. Decide for yourself.
hero.lead: Cropstar will not tell you which variety to sow, when to fertilise or what to spray. It shows you what changes when you change something — with the uncertainty and with the reasoning. So that you read your own ecosystem again, instead of trusting recommendations someone else made for you.

facts.numbersValue: a band, a source and a reason
facts.decisionValue: with the person in the field

independence.title: Independence begins with understanding
independence.p1: Variety, seeding rate, fertilisation, crop protection — every one of those decisions comes with a recommendation attached. Usually from someone with something to sell. That is comfortable for as long as the season goes to plan. In the year it does not, nobody is standing beside you explaining why.
independence.p2: A resilient farm is not built out of recommendations. It is built out of understanding. Once you know how water, nitrogen, roots and soil life interact on your own field, you make decisions that hold up in the difficult year — and you reach yields that stay stable, in step with nature rather than against it.
independence.p3: No software can replace that understanding, and Cropstar does not try. It wants to get the ball rolling: make relationships visible, play consequences through, keep a record of what you observed. The decision stays where it belongs.

principles.title: Four rules we hold ourselves to
principles.lead: Most programs hand you an answer and hide the path to it. We do the opposite. These four rules are review criteria, not slogans: anything that breaks one of them does not ship.

numbers.title: No bare numbers
numbers.body: 4.2 t/ha is a claim. 3.6 to 4.9 t/ha, computed from your weather and your soil, is information. Every value carries its uncertainty and its provenance — and says whether it was observed or computed.

scenarios.title: Scenarios, not recommendations
scenarios.body: You define the variants; Cropstar puts them side by side. No ranking, no “optimal”, no pre-filled value. The trade-off between yield, quality, cost and what stays in the soil is yours.

why.title: Always an answer to “why”
why.body: Water stress, nitrogen deficit, BBCH stage: whatever gets displayed can name the drivers behind it. What cannot be explained is not shown in the first place.

warnings.title: Warnings describe, they never prescribe
warnings.body: “Plant-available soil moisture has been below 40 % for twelve days.” Not “irrigate now.” You know your machinery, your soil and your contracts — the software does not.

explore.title: Change one thing. Watch what moves.
explore.lead: Two levers as they actually occur in the field: the rain you get, and the manure you spread. Every number carries its uncertainty and explains itself. Nothing here tells you what to do.

provenance.headline: Illustrative — not a simulation
provenance.detail: These numbers come from a hard-coded response surface for organically managed winter wheat on a silt loam in the Pannonian lowland. No model runs, and nothing was measured. They show the shape of a relationship, never a prediction for your field.

inputs.rainfallHelp: Rain from sowing to harvest. How much of it becomes plant-available is decided by your soil — not by the amount alone.
inputs.manureHelp: Fresh matter applied. Around 5 kg of total nitrogen per tonne, of which roughly a third becomes plant-available this season. The rest builds humus and works in later years.
inputs.ceiling: Above 34 t/ha the supply exceeds the 170 kg N/ha from livestock manure that the nitrate action programme permits per hectare and year.

outputs.coverNote: Fraction of soil shaded by the canopy at its peak (fCover).

diagnostics.waterStressNote: Days on which plant-available soil moisture sat below 40 % of the usable field capacity.
diagnostics.nDeficitNote: Days on which the crop would have needed more nitrogen than soil and manure could supply.
diagnostics.nExportNote: Derived from yield and crude protein, using a factor of 5.7.
diagnostics.nRemainingNegative: The grain removes more nitrogen than the manure delivered. The difference came out of the soil stock.
diagnostics.nRemainingPositive: The remainder stays in the system: as humus, in crop residues, and as a reserve for the following crop.

drivers.title: What moved this number
drivers.footnote: The shares are read off the same table: one lever is held still while the other is pushed to the edge of its range.
drivers.nitrogenReference: a field with no manure at all

explore.drawingAria: Stylised winter wheat reacting to the water and manure settings
explore.caption: Drawn at BBCH 75 — medium milk. The drawing follows the figures beside it: tiller number from ground cover, colour from nitrogen supply, droop from water supply, rooting depth from the days spent short of water. The pale dots in the soil are plant-available nitrogen.
explore.closing: Note what the toy deliberately refuses to do: mark one setting as the right one. Two farms can read the same bands and decide differently — because soil, rotation, livestock and marketing differ.

contact.title: Early access
contact.lead: There is no sign-in yet, because there is nothing behind it yet. What exists today: the levers above, an open repository and a plan.
contact.body: If you farm, advise or research — especially in Austria — write to us. We would rather build plot management, observations and field records around real practice than guess at them and rebuild later.
contact.subject: Cropstar early access
contact.privacy: No form, no tracking, no mailing list. Plain email — and your address stays in our inbox.

status.thenTitle: Then: plots, observations and field records
status.thenBody: Field boundaries, tasks and data entry — at the desk and in your jacket pocket.
status.laterTitle: Later: weather, satellite retrievals and a real crop model
status.laterBody: A process-based baseline first. A learned model only where it beats that baseline on real observations.
